did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah was brought to Ramah in chains, along with the exiles from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken to Babylon, and Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, released him there.
Did you know? Nebuzaradan explained the destruction of Jerusalem in terms similar to Jeremiah’s prophecies: the destruction came because the people had sinned against the Lord and had not obeyed him.
Did you know? After his release, Jeremiah was given a choice: to go to Babylon under Nebuzaradan’s protection, or to remain in the land and go wherever he considered good and right.
Did you know? Jeremiah chose to remain in the land and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, in order to live among the remnant of the people who remained in the land.

Did you know? Gedaliah encouraged the army officers and their men not to fear serving the Chaldeans, but to remain in the land and serve the king of Babylon, hoping that things would go well for them.
Did you know? Gedaliah urged the people to gather wine, summer fruit, and olive oil, store them in containers, and continue living in the towns they had taken and that remained under their control.

Did you know? The news that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah over them caused the Jews living in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other countries to return to the land of Judah.
Did you know? Johanan and the army officers warned Gedaliah that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill him, but Gedaliah did not believe them.
Did you know? Johanan offered to kill Ishmael secretly, arguing that doing so would prevent the Jews gathered around Gedaliah from being scattered and the remnant of Judah from being lost.
Did you know? Gedaliah rejected Johanan’s proposal in strong terms, declaring that the warning about Ishmael was a lie, even though Johanan was trying to protect him and the remnant of the people.
